evaluation.final_reason: Partial settlement: Agent D made concessions that reduced noise sources but did not stop the daily early shower. Key lines: Turn 5: Agent D: "I can make my lunch the night before to cut down on kitchen noise." Turn 7: Agent D: "For Sunday nights, I can do that. I'll shower the night before." Turn 27: Agent D: "Okay. I'm already pretty quick, but I'll make sure of it. And I don't use a hairdryer." These are D's concessions (making lunch at night; agreeing Sunday-night change; committing to quick showers and no hairdryer). They address some requests but leave the main incompatibility — D's daily morning shower at 4:45 — unresolved.
position_change_notes: Agent D softened position by offering practical concessions: meal prep at night (Turn 5), agreeing to Sunday-night change (Turn 7), and promising quick showers/no hairdryer (Turn 27).
Agent A accepted the Sunday-night accommodation (Turn 8).
Agent B initially requested multiple nights then reduced to asking for one night (Turn 11), but did not obtain additional concessions beyond those D already offered.
Agent C retained a firm complaint about daily disturbance but gained commitments on speed and hairdryer use; C did not accept eliminating the morning shower entirely.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1: Agent A: "That's very early... The sound carries a lot" vs Turn 2: Agent D: "I know. It's for my hospital shift. I have to leave by 5.30." A clear incompatibility between A's need for quiet and D's fixed early schedule is established.

Turn 3: Agent A: "I have client presentations at 9 a.m." and Turn 4: Agent B: "My exams are this month." More household members report stakes affected by early noise, increasing the scope of the conflict.

Turn 5: Agent D offers a mitigation: "I can make my lunch the night before to cut down on kitchen noise." Turn 6: Agent A asks as a follow-up for Sunday nights. The offer reduces some noise-source conflict but the core incompatibility (morning routine) remains unresolved.

Turn 7: Agent D: "For Sunday nights, I can do that. I'll shower the night before." Turn 8: Agent A: thanks. The specific Sunday-night request is accepted, but the broader issue of daily early showers is still outstanding.

Turn 9: Agent B requests additional nights: "Can you do the same for me on Monday and Wednesday nights?" Turn 10: Agent D refuses further concessions: "I really need that shower in the morning... I can't also give up my shower." Direct opposing demands persist.

Turn 11: Agent B softens requesting one night only. Turn 12: Agent C raises a broader concern: "I'm worried about being woken up every morning." The disagreement expands to daily disturbance and remains unresolved.

Turn 13: Agent D reiterates limits: "I really can't give it up more than the one night." Turn 16: Agent C: "the shower is still going to be loud." Positions (need for morning shower vs being woken daily) remain in strong opposition.

Turn 17: Agent D: "Some noise is just part of living in a flat." Turn 18: Agent C: "It's not 'some noise' when it's at 4:45..." Both sides restate the clash between D's necessity and others' need for sleep, hardening the disagreement.

Turn 21 (repeat): Agent C: same complaint about 4:45. Turn 22: Agent D: "It's the time I have to get up... I've already agreed to make my lunch the night before. The shower is all that's left, and I need it." No new concessions; core conflict persists.

Turn 23: Agent C requests practical limits: "can you just be as quick as possible? ... And don't use a hairdryer in there, please." Turn 27: Agent D agrees: "I'll make sure of it. And I don't use a hairdryer." D concedes on speed and hairdryer use, reducing but not eliminating the morning-noise issue.

Turn 28 & 31: Agent C offers thanks. No new substantive proposals or disputes. The partial accommodations already offered (night-before lunch, Sunday-night shower change, quick shower/no hairdryer) stand but the daily early-morning shower remains an unresolved incompatibility.
No public speech or observable action recorded. No further resolution; prior partial accommodations remain in place but the core early-morning noise conflict is not settled.

substantive_insights: Conflict arises from an incompatibility between a fixed early shift schedule and roommates' need for uninterrupted sleep for work/exams.
Partial, targeted accommodations (night-before lunch, one-night exception, no hairdryer, faster shower) reduce some impacts but do not resolve the structural schedule mismatch.

Different roommates prioritize different days: some need Sunday night quiet for Monday presentations, others need multiple nights — creating competing specific demands that a single simple concession cannot satisfy.
